new_statements.relation_note: Not in the READALL works list; downloaded because it is the primary phonology of exactly this variety (the introduction, p. 10, says the paper 'has been confined to the sub-dialect spoken in the barrio of Guinaang, in the municipality of Lubuagan', informants Juan Baluga and Ireniu M. Wansi, 1954-56). The Rosetta Project tags the item kmd (Majukayang Kalinga), which is a mis-tag; the text is Guinaang = lubu1243. The catalog record for Guinaang Kalinga has an empty rule field, so this fills it: contrastive stress, lexically distributed, penult vs final pairs, no rule stated.
new_statements.rule_in_words: Stress is phonemic (contrastive) in Guinaang Kalinga; minimal pairs differ by penultimate vs final stress (bálat 'banana' / balát 'broth'; sánga 'anger' / sangá 'branch'; kíwa 'jar-hanger' / kawá 'spider'). No placement rule is given; the author states stress had not yet been fully studied.
new_statements.exceptions: None beyond the statement that stress 'has not been fully studied as yet'. Orthographic note p. 11: a stressed syllable closed by glottal stop takes a circumflex, an unstressed one a grave accent.
new_statements.identity_note: Both Gieser works describe the sub-dialect of barrio Guinaang, municipality of Lubuagan, Kalinga (the language calls itself Kinalinga / Guininaang), i.e. lubu1243 = Lubuagan Kalinga (knb). The Rosetta Project mis-tags Gieser 1958 as kmd (Majukayang Kalinga); the text itself is Guinaang. The downloaded Reid 1971 excerpt is the Ilongot (Kakiduge:n / Bugkalut, ilk) page, not Kalinga; Reid 1971's own Guinaang Kalinga entry (phonological data from Gieser) was not accessible.

This construction has the general meaning of 'process' or 'procedure'. It is to be noted that stress occurs on the reduplicated syllable. [...] The preceding construction (man- + C1V1 + root) contrasts with three others that have the same reduplication but without stress on the reduplicated syllable."

new_statements.relation_note: Not in the READALL works list; already held by the project from the 2026-09-16 pass (ERIC/archive.org copy, public). Same variety (Guinaang, Lubuagan) and same author as Gieser 1958; the two agree exactly (three of the four 1987 minimal pairs are the 1958 pairs). Adds to the empty catalog rule: contrastive stress, penult vs final, plus a morphological stress contrast in reduplication.
new_statements.rule_in_words: Word stress is contrastive ('significant'), marked with an acute accent in the texts; minimal pairs oppose penultimate and final stress (bálat/balát, sánga/sangá, áwit/awít, áwa/awá). No general placement rule. Morphologically conditioned stress: in the man- + C1V1-reduplicated 'process' construction the reduplicated syllable is stressed, whereas the 'practitioner', 'continuous/plural action' and 'plural adjective' constructions have the same reduplication without stress on the reduplicant.
new_statements.exceptions: Stress on the reduplicated syllable distinguishes the man-C1V1- 'process/procedure' construction from three homophonous-looking reduplicated constructions (p. 126).
new_statements.identity_note: Both Gieser works describe the sub-dialect of barrio Guinaang, municipality of Lubuagan, Kalinga (the language calls itself Kinalinga / Guininaang), i.e. lubu1243 = Lubuagan Kalinga (knb). The Rosetta Project mis-tags Gieser 1958 as kmd (Majukayang Kalinga); the text itself is Guinaang. The downloaded Reid 1971 excerpt is the Ilongot (Kakiduge:n / Bugkalut, ilk) page, not Kalinga; Reid 1971's own Guinaang Kalinga entry (phonological data from Gieser) was not accessible.

audit.reasoning: (1) Quote check: the deciding quotation is verbatim in the Gieser 1958 scan we hold at sec. 1 and sec. 3.3, printed p. 19, as the locator says (page scan read). (2) Deciding source is a 1958 12-page SIL phonemic article by the variety's principal describer; Glottolog lists no reference grammar or later independent phonology for lubu1243 (the non-Gieser 'grammar sketch' entries are spurious title matches), and the author's own 1987 phonology appendix, downloaded now from archive.org (ERIC microfiche of SPL Philippine Texts 4, p. 116), restates stress as 'significant' with four minimal pairs (bálat/balát, sánga/sangá, áwit/awít, áwa/awá) and adds (p. 126) a morphologically conditioned stress-on-reduplicant contrast — fully consistent with the 'lexical' (contrastive, no positional rule) coding. (3) Remaining unheld items are Gieser 1972 Phonetica (paywalled DOI 10.1159/000259383) and the 1963 SI
